title: The quoted floor is not honoured across a real quote->execute gap: minOut is re-derived from live state at execution, so the guarantee silently collapses with it
description: _disposeShares re-derives minOut inline from live state at :245-246 rather than accepting or honouring the floor quoted by previewExitFor. _exitFloor (:127-135) and the inline recomputation (:245-246) are the SAME EXPRESSION by convention across three copies (the third is a test helper), an equality nothing enforces. The floor therefore holds ATOMICALLY and evaporates the moment a real quote->execute gap exists — which is the only mode in which a STATICCALL preview is useful.
impact: Silent ~99% under-delivery: 19,602e18 quoted at T1, 181.9e18 delivered at T2 — 0.93% of the guarantee, with no revert, no event and no signal. Census v1d_floorBreachesDeferred 35 direct / 1 market over r_deferredExits 35/13. This is the most severe SHAPE in the run.
attackPath: Two clients are funded on the market strategy.
A consumer STATICCALLs previewExitFor at T1 and records netGuaranteed = 19,602e18.
The OTHER client exits first, consuming shares.
The consumer executes at T2. _disposeShares recomputes minOut from live state, so the T1 floor is silently replaced by a much lower one.
181.9e18 is delivered against a 19,602e18 guarantee. No revert, no event, no signal.
recommendation: Make the floor ENFORCEABLE rather than advisory: pass the quoted netGuaranteed into withdraw as a caller-supplied minOut and revert if execution cannot meet it, instead of recomputing it inline. Landing L-29 (capture vault.redeem's return and compare it to the quoted floor) first converts the silent failures into loud ones as an interim mitigation.
whyNotMedium: Nobody sees the quote — zero consumers; the divergence is unobserved and unrelied-on today.

The delivery shortfall itself is already owner-accepted: 'debited for the requested amount regardless of what was received' is AYieldStrategy.sol:781-783 by explicit design ('shortfall accrues as yield'), and the FCFS-at-par socialization it implements is stable-staker 69c7666eee33698e... — wont-fix, 'intended design, confirmed by protocol owner'. What is NEW at cdd0743 is only that the protocol now publishes a number under the word 'guarantees' that this accepted design will not honour.

The PoC's two-exit-capable-client premise does not hold in the deployed wiring — CONFIRMED, not assumed: in the live ResumeStableStakerMigration broadcast (chain 1) each strategy receives setClient(..., true) for exactly two addresses, PhusdStableMinter (0x435B0A18...) and StableStaker (0xbce8ABC0...), and ONLY StableStaker receives setWithdrawer(true). One exit-capable client. The gap still opens on a price move alone, but the demonstrated 99% magnitude does not.
whyNotQA: The floor's atomic correctness is an UNENFORCED CONVENTION — the same expression copied across three places (:127-135, :245-246, t.sol:44-52; pattern D-5), an equality nothing checks. It holds atomically (256,000 forge + 209,901 medusa calls, no counterexample) and evaporates the moment the gap is real.
distinctness: LOAD-BEARING. Different harm from L-21 (silent vs revert), different root cause (the quote is not a snapshot), and DIFFERENT MITIGATION — the floor must become enforceable as a caller-supplied minOut, which L-21's AMM-quote fix does not deliver. Filing it under L-21 would let the wrong fix close it. It also fires on the DIRECT strategy (35 deferred breaches), which L-21 instance (a) does not touch at all.
escalationTrigger: Any consumer that PERSISTS a netGuaranteed across blocks — an off-chain keeper, or a two-phase totalWithdrawal flow => Medium (value leak, stated assumptions, external requirement = a price move in the gap). WATCH-17-03.
disclosure: stable-staker M-01 / 2b9a89d29c34df41aee609d0b5f2c6ae82c1e509877261424c2c20f317fbb0c3 (Medium, wont-fix), 'Par-exit front-run on the migration cushion.' triageReason verbatim: 'OWNER DECISION 2026-08-29, recorded in the owner's own terms. The finding is VALID — this is explicitly NOT a rejection on the merits and NOT a severity downgrade. It is closed wont-fix because the mitigation is OPERATIONAL rather than a code change, and is OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS REPO: the pause() -> initiateMigration() -> unpause() sequence belongs in the deployment script that performs the migration, which lives in phoenix-phase-2-staging. Nothing in stable-staker can fix it.' ADJACENT, NOT A DUPLICATE: 2b9a89d2... is a stable-staker buffer-ordering value transfer between stakers; this is a reflax quote->execute gap where the strategy's own floor is silently re-derived. Its wont-fix reasoning ('nothing in stable-staker can fix it') carries NO authority over reflax code, where the fix IS a code change. Not suppressed.
